record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.original_question: Resolve the uniqueness problem for Daróczy’s equation φ(x) = φ(x+1) + φ(x(x+1)) within the class of regularly varying functions in the sense of Karamata.

evidence.quote: It seems that it would be also interesting to answer the uniqueness problem for the Dar´oczy equation in the class of regularly varying functions in the sense of Karamata.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A function $\varphi:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is said to be regularly varying at infinity in the sense of Karamata with index $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ if $\varphi$ is measurable, eventually positive, and for every $\lambda>0$,
$$\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{\varphi(\lambda x)}{\varphi(x)}=\lambda^{\rho}.$$

Consider Daróczy's functional equation
$$\varphi(x)=\varphi(x+1)+\varphi\bigl(x(x+1)\bigr),\qquad x>0.$$

Determine whether the solution of this equation is unique (up to the natural normalization/scaling) within the class of functions that are regularly varying at infinity in the sense of Karamata. More precisely, classify all regularly varying functions $\varphi:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying the above equation.

status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes on Karamata's theory of regularly varying functions; no mention of Daróczy's equation uniqueness.
